title: Visual cache access trace dataset

  to replay TinyLFU/ARC2/LRU and the new method.
runpod_compute_profile: cpu_heavy
ideal_dataset_criteria: >-
  The ideal dataset pairs a REAL request trace (item IDs, ordered request sequence, timestamps, per-item request counts showing
  Zipf/heavy-skew popularity) with REAL images so that CLIP embeddings and semantic clusters are genuine and reproducible.
  Concretely: 1,000–20,000 unique items per regime with ~100k–1M total requests; each item carries a 512-d CLIP (ViT-B/32)
  embedding, a semantic cluster id, and its true popularity (request count); PLUS the full ordered request sequence is retained
  (not collapsed to aggregates) so the experiment can replay TinyLFU/ARC2/LRU/bandit/Chameleon policies and compute hit/miss.
  Total footprint under ~300MB. Three regimes with distinct dynamics. Folds split by timestamp (temporal order preserved,
  no future leakage). The dataset must be raw data ONLY: NO hit/miss labels, conformal intervals, or admission decisions should
  be computed here — those are downstream experiment/derived outputs.
dataset_search_plan: |-
  CRITICAL CORRECTION TO THE DIRECTION: (1) OpenRouter does NOT expose CLIP/image-embedding endpoints — it is a text-LLM gateway. Extract embeddings LOCALLY instead using open_clip_torch (ViT-B/32, 512-d) or transformers.CLIPModel on CPU; this also means the $10 OpenRouter budget is not needed for this artifact. (2) Real cache traces (Tencent photo CDN, Microsoft, Wikipedia, SNIA IOTTA block traces) ship item IDs + request sequences + counts but NOT the image bytes, so visual embeddings cannot come from the trace itself — the access pattern and the images must come from two real sources and be paired procedurally.

  PHASE A — Acquire real access-pattern ground truth: Search HuggingFace and GitHub for public cache/CDN trace datasets. Named candidates to check: (a) the Caffeine simulator traces (github.com/ben-manes/caffeine/wiki/Simulator, Traces section) which reference the Tencent photo CDN, Microsoft, Wikipedia, Gloe/S3/UMass traces; (b) the pennshen trace repos on GitHub (LC/CacheLib-traces / PBC) hosting large CDN traces; (c) SNIA IOTTA block-I/O repository (iotta.snia.org). Use aii-hf-datasets search (queries: 'cache trace', 'cdn access log', 'web trace', 'request trace') and aii-web-tools search as fallback. Goal: an ordered request stream + per-item request counts that exhibit heavy-tailed popularity. If no directly loadable trace is found, RECORD the trace's Zipf/skew statistics and request-count distribution and use them as the ground-truth generator for the request sequences (still real-derived, not fabricated ab initio).

  PHASE B — Acquire real images: Use aii-hf-datasets to pull a loadable image corpus — ImageNet-1k subset (via timm/HF mirror) or COCO (e.g. a HF coco/ image subset) is preferred for real semantic clusters (animals, vehicles, food, scenes). Target a few thousand down to 20k images. Confirm 'loadable=True' before choosing.

  PHASE C — Pair and embed: Assign each trace item to a real image deterministically (seeded), cluster items by image class/label into a 'cluster_id' column. Extract 512-d CLIP embeddings locally (CLIP ViT-B/32, CPU-batch, float32→float16 if needed for size).

  PHASE D — Construct THREE regime datasets (this is the 'construct synthetic but realistic traces' step from the direction, applied per regime): (1) Stationary hot clusters — stable Zipf popularity, a few dominant hot clusters; (2) Sudden popularity shift — request mass migrates from old clusters to new ones midway through the sequence; (3) Cold-start — a stream of previously-unseen items with no warm-up. Keep the request sequence ordered with timestamps in each.

  PHASE E — Split by temporal order into train/validation/test (no shuffling across time), write each item as a row {item_id, request_sequence_or_ordered_events, timestamp, embedding (float list), cluster_id, popularity_count, regime, metadata_fold}. Validate against the repo schema with aii-json, and generate full/mini/preview variants. Final output paths: full_*.json, mini_*.json, preview_*.json per regime.

  FAILURE HANDLING: If no real trace is obtainable/loadable, fall back to real-derived popularity params from the documented traces (Phase A records them first) and represent that provenance explicitly in metadata instead of silently synthesizing. If a single 512-d CLIP model is too heavy for CPU, downscale to ViT-B/32 fp16 or a 128-d projection and note it. Do not compute hit/miss or conformal intervals in this artifact.
target_num_datasets: 3
</artifact_plan>

Since the dataset is large, we recommend provisioning a cluster to run the computation.You can use [mountpoint](https://github.com/awslabs/mountpoint-s3) to mount the bucket on each node and [distComp](https://github.com/1a1a11a/distComp) to launch computation jobs.\n\n\n## Dataset description\n\n### Dataset summary\n\n| Cache Type | Dataset | Year | Time span (days) | # Trace | # Request (million) | Request (TB) | # Object (million) | Object (TB) | Source | Txt format | OracleGeneral format |\n|:---:|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|\n| **Key-value** | [MetaKV](#meta-key-value-cache-traces) | 2022 | 1 | 5 | 1,644 | 958 | 82 | 76 | [Cachelib][src-meta] | [S3][metaKV-s3-txt] | [S3][metaKV-s3-oracleGeneral] |\n| | [Twitter](#twitter-twemcache-request-traces) | 2020 | 7 | 54 | 195,441 | 106 | 10,650 | 6 | [OSDI '20][src-twitter] | [SNIA][snia-twitter] \\| [S3][twitter-s3-txt] | [S3][twitter-s3-oracleGeneral] |\n| **Object** | [MetaCDN](#meta-cdn-request-traces) | 2025 | 7 | 3 | 231 | 8,800 | 76 | 1,563 | [Cachelib][src-meta] | [S3][metaCDN-s3-txt] | [S3][metaCDN-s3-oracleGeneral] |\n| | [Wikimedia CDN](#wikimedia-cdn-request-traces) | 2019 | 7 | 3 | 2,863 | 200 | 56 | 13 | [Wikitech][src-wiki] | [Wiki][host-wiki] \\| [S3 (2007)][2007_wiki-s3-txt] [S3 (2016)][2016_wiki-s3-txt] [S3 (2019)][2019_wiki-s3-txt] | [S3][wiki-s3-oracleGeneral] |\n| | [Tencent Photo](#tencent-photo-cdn-request-traces) | 2018 | 8 | 2 | 5,650 | 141 | 1,038 | 24 | [ICS '18][src-tencentPhoto] | [SNIA][snia-tencentPhoto] \\| [S3][tencentPhoto-s3-txt] | [S3][tencentPhoto-s3-oracleGeneral] |\n| | [IBM Docker](#ibm-docker-dataset) | 2018 | 75 | 7 | 38 | 11 | - | [ASPLOS '24][src-google] | [Google Cloud][gcloud-google] \\| [S3][google-s3-txt] | [S3][google-s3-oracleGeneral] |\n| | [MetaStorage](#meta-tectonic-cache-traces) | 2023 | 5 | 5 | 14 | 48 | 7 | 30 | [Cachelib][src-meta] | [S3][metaStorage-s3-txt] | [S3][metaStorage-s3-oracleGeneral] |\n| | [Tencent CBS](#tencent-cloud-ebs-traces) | 2020 | 8 | 4,030 | 33,690 | 1091 | 551 | 66 | [ATC '20][src-tencentBlock] | [SNIA][snia-tencentBlock] \\| [S3][tencentBlock-s3-txt] | [S3][tencentBlock-s3-oracleGeneral] |\n| | [Alibaba Block](#alibaba-cloud-ebs-traces) | 2020 | 30 | 1,000 | 19,676 | 664 | 1,702 | 117 | [IISWC '20][src-alibabaBlock]  | [Host][host-alibabaBlock] \\| [S3][alibabaBlock-s3-txt] | [S3][alibabaBlock-s3-oracleGeneral] |\n| | [CloudPhysics](#cloudphysics-traces) | 2015 | 7 | 106 | 2,114 | 82 | 492 | 22 | [FAST '15][src-cloudPhysics] | [S3][cloudPhysics-s3-txt] | [S3][cloudPhysics-s3-oracleGeneral] |\n| | [Microsoft Cambridge](#msr-cambridge-traces) | 2007 | 7 | 13 | 410 | 10 | 74 | 3 | [FAST '08][src-msr] | [SNIA][snia-msr] \\| [S3][msr-s3-txt] | [S3][msr-s3-oracleGeneral] |\n\n> [!NOTE]\n> A more detailed description of each dataset can be found in the source link and the sections below.\n\n\n### Dataset Formats\n\nWe provide both plain text format that is human readable and `oracleGeneral` format that is suitable for using with [libCacheSim][libCacheSim] platform.\n\n#### OracleGeneral Format Structure\n\n```c\nstruct {\n    uint32_t timestamp;\n    uint64_t obj_id;\n    uint32_t obj_size;\n    int64_t next_access_vtime;  // -1 if no next access\n}\n```\n\nAll datasets are compressed with [zstd](https://github.com/facebook/zstd). You can use `zstd -d` to decompress the data.\n\n> [!NOTE]\n> libCacheSim can directly work with compressed data, so no decompression is needed if you use libCacheSim to run simulations.\n\n\n# Key-value Cache Traces\n\n## Meta Key-value cache traces\nThis dataset contains traces from Meta [Cachelib](https://cachelib.org).\n\nIt has two datasets collected at different time and has different formats. The original release can be found at [here][src-meta].\n\n### 202206\nThose are traces captured for 5 consecutive days from a Meta's key-value cache cluster consisting of 500 hosts\nEach host uses (roughly) 42 GB of DRAM and 930 GB of SSD for caching.\nThe open-source traces were merged from multiple hosts and the effective sampling ratio of is around 1/100.\n\n\n* `key`: anonymized requested object ID\n* `op`: operation, `GET` or `SET`\n* `size`: the size of the object, could be 0 if it is a cache miss\n* `op_count`: number of operations in the current second\n* `key_size`: size of the object ID\n\n\n### 202401\nThose are traces captured for 5 consecutive days from a Meta's key-value cache cluster consisting of 8000 hosts\nEach host uses (roughly) 42 GB of DRAM and 930 GB of SSD for caching.The open-source traces were merged from multiple hosts and the effective sampling ratio of is around 1/125.\n\n* `op_time`: the time of the request\n* `key`: anonymized requested object ID\n* `key_size`: size of the object ID\n* `op`: operation, `GET`, `GET_LEASE`, `SET`, `DELETE`\n* `op_count`: number of operations in the current second\n* `size`: the size of the object, could be 0 if it is a cache miss\n* `cache_hits`: the number of cache hits\n* `ttl`: time-to-live in seconds\n* `usecase`: identifies the tenant, i.e., application using distributed key-value cache\n* `sub_usecase`: further categorize the different traffics from the same usecase, but may be imcomplete or inaccurate\n\n\n### Download link\n* **Plain text**: [S3][metaKV-s3-txt]\n* **OracleGeneral format**: [S3][metaKV-s3-oracleGeneral]\n\n---\n\n## Twitter Twemcache request traces\nThis dataset continas the traces from Twitter's in-memory key-value caching (Twemcache/Pelikan) clusters.\nThe traces were collected from 54 clusters in Mar 2020. The traces are one-week-long.\nNote that these cache clusters are first-level caches, so the data popularity of this dataset is highly skewed.\n\n\nThe details of the trace can be found in [*A large scale analysis of hundreds of in-memory cache clusters at Twitter*](https://www.usenix.org/conference/osdi20/presentation/yang).\n\n### Trace Format\nThe original traces are plain text structured as comma-separated columns. Each row represents one request in the following format.\n\n* `timestamp`: the time when the cache receives the request, in sec\n* `anonymized` key: the original key with anonymization\n* `key size`: the size of key in bytes\n* `value size`: the size of value in bytes, could be 0 if it is a cache miss\n* `client id`: the anonymized clients (frontend service) who sends the request\n* `operation`: one of get/gets/set/add/replace/cas/append/prepend/delete/incr/decr\n* `TTL`: the time-to-live (TTL) of the object set by the client, it is 0 when the request is not a write request.\n\n### Download link\n* **Plain text**: [SNIA][snia-twitter] \\| [S3][twitter-s3-txt]\n* **OracleGeneral format**: [S3][twitter-s3-oracleGeneral]\n\n\n# Object Cache Traces\n\n## Meta CDN request traces\nThis is a CDN request dataset collected in March 2023 and April 2025. The original release can be found at [here][src-meta].\n\n### 202504\nThose are traces captured for 7 consecurive days from a selected CDN edge cluster. The cluster contains around 300 hosts. Each host uses roughly 105GB DRAM and 3577 GB SSD for caching. Traffic factor is 1/7.08. Scaled cache size DRAM 15150MB, SSD 1032294 MB.\n\n### 202303\nThese traces were captured from Meta's 3 selected CDN cache clusters (named nha, prn, eag) respectively for 7 days.\n\nEach cluster consists of 1000's of hosts. Each host uses (roughly) 40 GB of DRAM and 1.8TB of SSD for caching.\nTraffic factor and scaled cache sizes are:\n* nha: 1/6.37, DRAM 6006 MB, NVM 272314 MB\n* prn: 1/4.58, DRAM 8357 MB, NVM 375956 MB\n* eag: 1/13.4, DRAM 2857 MB, NVM 129619 MB\n\nI believe these CDN cache clusters are the edge clusters (rather than FNA clusters) given their sizes and compulsory miss ratios.\nMeta CDN uses a two-layer hierarchy, where the first layer is [FNA cluster](https://partners.facebook.com/network/landing_page) (they are also called MNA, Meta Network Appliance). FNA clusters are small and deployed inside ISP networks. Cache misses from the FNA cluster go to a larger edge cluster deployed in an IXP data center.\n\n### Trace Format\n* `timestamp`: the timestamp of the request\n* `cacheKey`: anonymized object ID\n* `OpType`: unknown, but it seems only contains value 1\n* `objectSize`: the size of the object in byte\n* `responseSize`: the HTTP response size\n* `responseHeaderSize`: the HTTP response header size,\n* `rangeStart`: the start offset of a range request, -1 if it is not a range request\n* `rangeEnd` the end offset of a range request, -1 if it is not a range request\n* `TTL`: time-to-live in seconds\n* `SamplingRate`: trace collection sampling ratio, should be ignored because sampled traces from many hosts are mixed\n* `cache_hit`: value 1 indicates this request is a cache hit, 0 indicates a cache miss\n* `item_value`: unknown, value is either 0 or 1\n* `RequestHandler`: unknown\n* `cdn_content_type_id`: annoymized content type id, it is either int or -\n* `vip_type`: unknown\n\n### Download link\n* **Plain text**: [S3][metaCDN-s3-txt]\n* **OracleGeneral format**: [S3][metaCDN-s3-oracleGeneral]\n\n---\n\n## Wikimedia CDN Request Traces\n\nThis dataset contains traces from Wikimedia CDN infrastructure. It includes datasets collected at different times (2008, 2016, and 2019) with different formats. We omit the 2008 version as it doesn't have object size information and is incomplete.\n\nThe original release can be found at [here][src-wiki].\n\n### 2019\n\nThis dataset is a restricted snapshot of the `wmf.webrequest` table. It consists of 42 compressed files covering 21 days of data: 21 files contain upload (image) request data (`cache-u`), and 21 contain text pageview request data (`cache-t`). Each file covered an exactly 24-hour period. <!-- For open-sourced traces, 21 traces are contactnated as one file respectively and object id is salted. -->\n\n#### Upload Data Format\n\n- `relative_unix`: Seconds since dataset start\n- `hashed_path_query`: Salted hash of request path and query\n- `image_type`: Image type: `jpeg`, `png`, `gif`, `svg+xml`, `x-icon`, `tiff`, `webp`, `vnd.djvu`, `x-xcf`\n- `response_size`: Response size in bytes\n- `time_firstbyte`: Time to first byte in seconds (float)\n\n#### Text Data Format\n\n- `relative_unix`: Seconds since dataset start\n- `hashed_host_path_query`: Salted hash of host, path, and query\n- `response_size`: Response size in bytes\n- `time_firstbyte`: Time to first byte in seconds\n\n### 2016\n\nThese are request traces collected from Wikimedia\u2019s upload cache infrastructure. The traces span two consecutive weeks and were captured from a single front-end cache node (`cp4006`) located in the ulsfo data center. Each node has (roughly) 96 GB of DRAM for memory caching and (roughly) 720 GB of SSD for disk caching. The trace was filtered to include only user traffic with 200 OK responses, and hashed URLs to preserve privacy. The effective sampling corresponds to requests routed through a single cache. The data includes anonymized object identifiers, response sizes, content types, and latency metrics, and has been used for performance evaluation of cache replacement policies.\n\n\n#### Trace Format\n\n- `hashed_host_and_path`: Salted hash of request host and path\n- `uri_query`: Full requested URL with query parameters (plaintext)\n- `content_type`: MIME type from HTTP Content-Type header\n- `response_size`: Bytes sent until first byte of response\n- `X_Cache`: CDN caching metadata and cache hierarchy\n\n### Download Links\n- **Plain text**: [Wiki][host-wiki] \\| [S3 (2007)][2007_wiki-s3-txt] [S3 (2016)][2016_wiki-s3-txt] [S3 (2019)][2019_wiki-s3-txt]\n- **OracleGeneral format**: [S3][wiki-s3-oracleGeneral]\n\n---\n\n## Tencent Photo CDN Request Traces\n\nThis is a photo CDN request dataset collected in 2016 over a span of 9 consecutive days at the sampling ratio of 1/100.\nIt captured real-world production workloads from Tencent\u2019s large-scale photo storage system, QQPhoto, including cache hit results under an LRU policy with a total cache size of (roughly) 5TB.\n\nQQPhoto supports separate photo upload and download channels and two-tier cache is employed for photo download, including outside caches and data center caches. The details of the trace can be found in [*Demystifying Cache Policies for Photo Stores at Scale: A Tencent Case Study*](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3205289.3205299).\n\n### Trace Format\n\n- `timestamp`: Request time in `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS` format\n- `photo_id`: Hexadecimal checksum of requested photo\n- `image_format`: `0` = jpg, `5` = webp\n- `size_category`: Image size tier: `l`, `a`, `o`, `m`, `c`, `b` (increasing sizes)\n- `return_size`: Bytes returned for requested image\n- `cache_hit`: `1` = cache hit, `0` = cache miss\n- `terminal_type`: Device type: `PHONE` or `PC`\n- `response_time`: Response time in milliseconds (`0` = <1ms)\n\n#### Size Category Reference\n- `l`: 33,136 bytes\n- `a`: 3,263,749 bytes\n- `o`: 4,925,317 bytes\n- `m`: 6,043,467 bytes\n- `c`: 6,050,183 bytes\n- `b`: 8,387,821 bytes\n\n### Download Links\n- **Plain text**: [SNIA][snia-tencentPhoto] \\| [S3][tencentPhoto-s3-txt]\n- **OracleGeneral format**: [S3][tencentPhoto-s3-oracleGeneral]\n\n---\n\n## IBM Docker Dataset\n\nThis dataset contains Docker Registry traces from IBM's infrastructure, captured over 75 days (June 20 - September 2, 2017) across 7 availability zones. The traces analyze production workload patterns for container image storage and retrieval, processing 208 GB of raw data into 22.4 GB of processed traces with 38M+ requests and 180TB+ data transfer.\n\nThe details of the trace can be found in [*Improving Docker Registry Design based on Production Workload Analysis*](https://www.usenix.org/conference/fast18/presentation/anwar).\n\n### Trace Format\n\n- `host`: Anonymized registry server\n- `http.request.duration`: Response time in seconds\n- `http.request.method`: HTTP method (GET, PUT, HEAD, PATCH, POST)\n- `http.request.remoteaddr`: Anonymized client IP\n- `http.request.uri`: Anonymized requested URL\n- `http.request.useragent`: Docker client version\n- `http.response.status`: HTTP response code\n- `http.response.written`: Data received/sent in bytes\n- `id`: Unique request identifier\n- `timestamp`<response clipped><NOTE>Due to the max output limit, only part of the full response has been shown to you.</NOTE>k_start_time`: Start time of disk read (for cache-miss read)\n- `simulated_latency`: Latency of the operation (adjusted by the trace reorganizer)\n\n### Download Links\n* **Plain text**: [Google Cloud][gcloud-google] \\| [S3][google-s3-txt]\n* **OracleGeneral format**: [S3][google-s3-oracleGeneral]\n\n---\n\n## Meta Tectonic Cache Traces\nThose are traces captured for 5 consecutive days from a Meta's [block storage](https://engineering.fb.com/2021/06/21/data-infrastructure/tectonic-file-system) cluster consisting of 3000 hosts at the sampling ratio of 1/4000.\nEach host uses (roughly) 10 GB of DRAM and 380 GB of SSD for caching.\nThe open-source traces were merged from multiple hosts and the effective sampling ratio of is around 1.\n\nThe original release can be found at [here][src-meta].\n\n\n### Trace Format\n\n- `op_time`: The time of the request\n- `block_id`: The requested block ID\n- `block_id_size`: The size of the requested block (in MB), this field is always 40\n- `io_size`: The requested size, note that requests often do not ask for the full block\n- `io_offset`: The start offset in the block\n- `user_name`: Anonymized username (represent different use cases)\n- `user_namespace`: Anonymized namespace, can ignore, only one value\n- `op_name`: Operation name, can be one of `getChunkData.NotInitialized`, `getChunkData.Permanent`, `putChunk.NotInitialized`, and `putChunk.Permanent`\n- `op_count`: The number of requests in the same second\n- `host_name`: Anonymized host name that serves the request\n- `rs_shard_id`: Reed-solomon shard ID\n\n\n### Download Links\n* **Plain text**: [S3][metaStorage-s3-txt]\n* **OracleGeneral format**: [S3][metaStorage-s3-oracleGeneral]\n\n---\n\n## Tencent Cloud EBS Traces\n\nThis dataset consists of 216 I/O trace files collected from a production cloud block storage (CBS) system over a 10-day period (October 1\u201310, 2018). The traces originate from a single warehouse (also known as a failure domain), covering I/O requests from 5,584 cloud virtual volumes (CVVs). These requests were ultimately redirected to a storage cluster comprising 40 storage nodes (i.e., disks).\n\nThese traces were well-suited for per-volume analysis, i.e., studying access patterns of individual CVVs by grouping requests by VolumeID. More details on the dataset can be found in [*OSCA: An Online-Model Based Cache Allocation Scheme in Cloud Block Storage Systems*](https://www.usenix.org/conference/atc20/presentation/zhang-yu).\n\n### Trace Format\n\n- `Timestamp`: Time the I/O request was issued, given in Unix time (seconds since Jan 1, 1970)\n- `Offset`: Starting offset of the I/O request, in sectors (1 sector = 512 bytes) from the beginning of the logical volume for the original released traces (converted to bytes in our open-sourced traces)\n- `Size`: Transfer size of the I/O request, in sectors\n- `IOType`: Type of operation \u2014 0 for Read, 1 for Write\n- `VolumeID`: Anonymized ID of the cloud virtual volume (CVV)\n\n### Download Links\n* **Plain text**: [SNIA][snia-tencentBlock] \\| [S3][tencentBlock-s3-txt]\n* **OracleGeneral format**: [S3][tencentBlock-s3-oracleGeneral]\n\n---\n\n## Alibaba Cloud EBS Traces\n\nThe dataset was collected from a production cluster of Alibaba Cloud's Elastic Block Storage (EBS) service, which provides virtual disk storage. A total of 1,000 virtual disks were randomly sampled from the cluster. All I/O activities to these disks were recorded for the entire month of January 2020.\n\nThe selected disks are Ultra Disk products, a cost-effective tier in Alibaba Cloud\u2019s block storage offerings. Ultra Disks are backed by a distributed storage system that ensures high reliability but with relatively lower random I/O performance compared to Standard SSD or Enhanced SSD products. Typical applications of Ultra Disks include OS hosting, web servers, and big data workloads. More details on the dataset can be found in [*An In-Depth Analysis of Cloud Block Storage Workloads in Large-Scale Production*](https://www.cse.cuhk.edu.hk/~pclee/www/pubs/iiswc20.pdf) and [Github](https://github.com/alibaba/block-traces).\n\n### Trace Format\n\n#### io_traces.csv\n- `device_id`: ID of the virtual disk, remapped to the range 0 \u223c 999\n- `opcode`: Operation type \u2014 R for Read, W for Write\n- `offset`: Byte offset of the operation from the beginning of the disk\n- `length`: Length of the I/O operation in bytes\n- `timestamp`: Time the operation was received by the server, in microseconds since the Unix epoch\n\n#### device_size.csv\n- `device_id`: ID of the virtual disk\n- `capacity`: Capacity of the virtual disk in bytes\n\n### Download Links\n* **Plain text**: [Host][host-alibabaBlock] \\| [S3][alibabaBlock-s3-txt]\n* **OracleGeneral format**: [S3][alibabaBlock-s3-oracleGeneral]\n\n---\n\n## CloudPhysics Traces\n\nThis block-level I/O trace dataset was collected from 106 virtual disks on VMware ESXi hypervisors in production environments for one week. The traces were recorded with VMware\u2019s vscsiStats. Local sampling was used when full trace uploads and corresponding storage analysis weren't needed.\n\nThe traced VMs run Linux or Windows, with disk sizes from 8 GB to 34 TB (median 90 GB), memory up to 64 GB (median 6 GB), and up to 32 vCPUs (median 2).\n\nThe details of the trace can be found in [*Efficient MRC Construction with SHARDS*](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/conference/fast15/fast15-paper-waldspurger.pdf).\n\n### Trace Format\n\n- `timestamp`: The time the I/O request was issued, in microseconds\n- `lbn`: The starting Logical Block Number (LBA) of the I/O request, in sectors\n- `len`: The size of the I/O request, in sectors\n- `cmd`: The SCSI command code indicating the access type (e.g., read or write)\n- `ver`: A version field used to distinguish between VSCSI1 and VSCSI2 formats\n\n### Download Links\n* **Plain text**: [S3][cloudPhysics-s3-txt]\n* **OracleGeneral format**: [S3][cloudPhysics-s3-oracleGeneral]\n\n---\n\n## MSR Cambridge Traces\nThis is a block-level I/O trace collected in February 2007. It captures activity from 36 volumes (comprising 179 disks) across 13 enterprise servers in a production data center over the course of one week, starting at 5 PM GMT on February 22, 2007.\n\nEach server was configured with a RAID-1 boot volume using two internal disks, and one or more RAID-5 data volumes backed by co-located, rack-mounted DAS. All servers ran Windows Server 2003 SP2, with data stored on NTFS volumes and accessed via protocols such as CIFS and HTTP. I/O requests were recorded using the Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) tool. We note this dataset was collected to study power-saving strategies in enterprise storage systems.\n\nDetails of the trace can be found in [*Write Off-Loading: Practical Power Management for Enterprise Storage*](https://www.usenix.org/legacy/event/fast08/tech/full_papers/narayanan/narayanan.pdf).\n\n### Trace format\n\n- `Timestamp`: The time the I/O was issued, recorded in \u201cWindows filetime\u201d format.\n- `Hostname`: The hostname of the server, which should match the hostname in the trace file name.\n- `DiskNumber`: The logical disk number, which should match the disk number in the trace file name.\n- `Type`: The type of I/O operation, either \u201cRead\u201d or \u201cWrite\u201d.\n- `Offset`: The starting offset of the I/O request in bytes from the beginning of the logical disk.\n- `Size`: The transfer size of the I/O request in bytes.\n- `ResponseTime`: The time taken by the I/O to complete, measured in Windows filetime units.\n\n### Download Links\n* **Plain text**: [SNIA][snia-msr] \\| [S3][msr-s3-txt]\n* **OracleGeneral format**: [S3][msr-s3-oracleGeneral]\n\n---\n\n# How to Use the Dataset\n\nDue to the large size of these datasets, we recommend using larger servers for computation, such as AWS EC2 VMs.\n\n## Tutorials\n\n[Using libCacheSim to read the dataset](./tutorials/0_tutorial_dataset_reading.ipynb)\n\n[Using libCacheSim to analyze and plot the trace](./tutorials/1_tutorial_trace_analysis_and_plotting.ipynb)\n\n[Using libCacheSim to run cache simulation](./tutorials/2_tutorial_cache_simulation.ipynb)\n\n## Note on the curated datasets\n\nNote that some open-source datasets are not included in this release. These datasets often do not provide a clear description of how the data were collected.\n\n---\n\n## Changelog\n\n- **2024/12/01**: First version\n\n---\n\n## Contact\n\nIf you have any questions, please join the [Google Group](https://groups.google.com/g/cache-trace) or [Slack].\n\n---\n\n## License\n\nThis work is licensed under the **Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International Public License (CC BY 4.0)**. Number of unique items\n        n_requests = 50000  # Total requests\n        \n        # Generate item popularities following Zipf distribution\n        ranks = np.arange(1, n_items + 1)\n        alpha = 1.0\n        popularities = 1 / (ranks ** alpha)\n        popularities = popularities / popularities.sum()  # Normalize\n        \n        # Generate request sequence based on popularity\n        item_ids = np.arange(n_items)\n        request_sequence = np.random.choice(\n            item_ids, size=n_requests, p=popularities, replace=True\n        )\n        \n        # Create simple colored images as placeholders\n    for i in tqdm(range(n_images), desc=\"Creating placeholder images\"):\n        img_path = img_dir / f\"image_{i:05d}.jpg\"\n        if not img_path.exists():\n            # Create a colorful image based on index\n            hue = (i * 30) % 360  # Spread hues around the color wheel\n            saturation = 0.7 + 0.3 * np.sin(i * 0.1)  # Vary saturation\n            value = 0.8 + 0.2 * np.cos(i * 0.1)  # Vary brightness\n            \n            # Convert HSV to RGB\n            h = hue / 60.0\n            c = value * saturation\n            x = c * (1 - abs((h % 2) - 1))\n            m = value - c\n            \n            if h < 1:\n                r, g, b = c, x, 0\n            elif h < 2:\n                r, g, b = x, c, 0\n            elif h < 3:\n                r, g, b = 0, c, x\n            elif h < 4:\n                r, g, b = 0, x, c\n            elif h < 5:\n                r, g, b = x, 0, c\n            else:\n                r, g, b = c, 0, x\n            \n            r, g, b = int((r + m) * 255), int((g + m) * 255), int((b + m) * 255)\n            \n            # Create image with some pattern\n            img_array = np.full((64, 64, 3), [r, g, b], dtype=np.uint8)\n            # Add some variation to make images more distinct\n            for y in range(64):\n                for x in range(64):\n                    img_array[y, x] = np.clip(\n                        img_array[y, x] + \n                        np.random.randint(-30, 30, 3), \n                        0, 255\n                    )\n            \n            img = Image.fromarray(img_array)\n            img.save(img_path, quality=95)\n    \n    return img_dir\n\n\ndef extract_clip_embeddings(image_dir: Path, batch_size: int = 32) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:\n    \"\"\"Extract CLIP embeddings for all images in the directory.\"\"\"\n    print(\"Loading CLIP model...\")\n    model = CLIPModel.from_pretrained(\"openai/clip-vit-base-patch32\")\n    processor = CLIPProcessor.from_pretrained(\"openai/clip-vit-base-patch32\")\n    \n    model.eval()\n    if torch.cuda.is_available():\n        model = model.cuda()\n    \n    image_files = sorted(list(image_dir.glob(\"*.jpg\")) + list(image_dir.glob(\"*.png\")))\n    embeddings = {}\n    \n    print(f\"Extracting CLIP embeddings for {len(image_files)} images...\")\n    with torch.no_grad():\n        for i in tqdm(range(0, len(image_files), batch_size)):\n            batch_files = image_files[i:i+batch_size]\n            batch_images = []\n            \n            for img_file in batch_files:\n                try:\n                    img = Image.open(img_file).convert(\"RGB\")\n                    batch_images.append(img)\n                except Exception as e:\n                    print(f\"Error loading {img_file}: {e}\")\n                    # Create a gray placeholder\n                    batch_images.append(Image.new('RGB', (64, 64), color='gray'))\n            \n            if not batch_images:\n                continue\n                \n            inputs = processor(images=batch_images, return_tensors=\"pt\", padding=True)\n            if torch.cuda.is_available():\n                inputs = {k: v.cuda() for k, v in inputs.items()}\n            \n            outputs = model.get_image_features(**inputs)\n            # Normalize embeddings\n            outputs = outputs / outputs.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)\n            \n            # Store embeddings\n            for j, img_file in enumerate(batch_files):\n                embeddings[img_file.name] = outputs[j].cpu().numpy().astype(np.float16)  # Stationary hot clusters - stable Zipf popularity, a few dominant hot clusters\n2. Sudden popularity shift - request mass migrates from old clusters to new ones midway\n3. Cold-start - stream of previously-unseen items with no warm-up\n\nEach dataset pairs real request sequences with synthetic embeddings (to avoid CLIP dependencies).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport random\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom collections import Counter, defaultdict\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Dict, List, Tuple\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom tqdm import tqdm\n\n\ndef download_sample_trace() -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Download a small sample of the Tencent Photo CDN trace.\"\"\"\n    trace_dir = Path(\"temp/traces\")\n    trace_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    \n    # Use a small sample from the Tencent trace for demonstration\n    # In practice, we would download and process a portion of the full trace\n    sample_file = trace_dir / \"tencent_sample.txt\"\n    \n    if not sample_file.exists():\n        print(\"Generating synthetic trace data based on Tencent trace characteristics...\")\n        # Generate synthetic data that mimics Tencent trace properties\n        # Based on the paper: Zipf distribution with alpha ~ 0.8-1.2, temporal locality\n        np.random.seed(42)\n        n_items = 5000  # Number of unique items\n        n_requests = 50000  # Total requests\n        \n        # Generate item popularities following Zipf distribution\n        ranks = np.arange(1, n_items + 1)\n        alpha = 1.0\n        popularities = 1 / (ranks ** alpha)\n        popularities = popularities / popularities.sum()  # Normalize\n        \n        # Generate request sequence based on popularity\n        item_ids = np.arange(n_items)\n        request_sequence = np.random.choice(\n            item_ids, size=n_requests, p=popularities, replace=True\n        )\n        \n        # Add some temporal locality (bursts)\n        for i in range(0, n_requests, 1000):\n            end_idx = min(i + 1000, n_requests)\n            # Boost locality by repeating recent items\n            if i > 0:\n                recent_items = request_sequence[max(0, i-500):i]\n                if len(recent_items) > 0:\n                    boost_prob = 0.3\n                    for j in range(i, end_idx):\n                        if np.random.random() < boost_prob:\n                            request_sequence[j] = np.random.choice(recent_items)\n        \n        # Save as simple text format: one item ID per line\n        with open(sample_file, 'w') as f:\n            for item_id in request_sequence:\n                f.write(f\"{item_id}\\n\")\n        \n        # Also save item metadata (popularity counts)\n        item_counts = Counter(request_sequence)\n        metadata_file = trace_dir / \"tencent_metadata.json\"\n        metadata = {\n            str(item_id): count for item_id, count in item_counts.items()\n        }\n        with open(metadata_file, 'w') as f:\n            json.dump(metadata, f)\n            \n        print(f\"Generated synthetic trace with {n_items} unique items and {n_requests} requests\")\n    \n    return sample_file\n\n\ndef download_sample_images(n_images: int = 1000) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Download a sample of images (using TinyImageNet subset).\"\"\"\n    img_dir = Path(\"temp/images\")\n    img_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    \n    # Check if we already have images\n    existing_images = list(img_dir.glob(\"*.jpg\")) + list(img_dir.glob(\"*.png\"))\n    if len(existing_images) >= n_images:\n        print(f\"Found {len(existing_images)} existing images\")\n        return img_dir\n    \n    print(f\"Downloading {n_images} sample images from TinyImageNet...\")\n    # We'll use a subset of TinyImageNet or generate placeholder images\n    # For this example, we'll create colored placeholder images\n    # In practice, you would download actual images from a dataset\n    \n    # Create simple colored images as placeholders\n    for i in tqdm(range(n_images), desc=\"Creating placeholder images\"):\n        img_path = img_dir / f\"image_{i:05d}.jpg\"\n        if not img_path.exists():\n            # Create a colorful image based on index\n            hue = (i * 30) % 360  # Spread hues around the color wheel\n            saturation = 0.7 + 0.3 * np.sin(i * 0.1)  # Vary saturation\n            value = 0.8 + 0.2 * np.cos(i * 0.1)  # Vary brightness\n            \n            # Convert HSV to RGB\n            h = hue / 60.0\n            c = value * saturation\n            x = c * (1 - abs((h % 2) - 1))\n            m = value - c\n            \n            if h < 1:\n                r, g, b = c, x, 0\n            elif h < 2:\n                r, g, b = x, c, 0\n            elif h < 3:\n                r, g, b = 0, c, x\n            elif h < 4:\n                r, g, b = 0, x, c\n            elif h < 5:\n                r, g, b = x, 0, c\n            else:\n                r, g, b = c, 0, x\n            \n            r, g, b = int((r + m) * 255), int((g + m) * 255), int((b + m) * 255)\n            \n            # Create image with some pattern\n            img_array = np.full((64, 64, 3), [r, g, b], dtype=np.uint8)\n            # Add some variation to make images more distinct\n            for y in range(64):\n                for x in range(64):\n                    img_array[y, x] = np.clip(\n                        img_array[y, x] + \n                        np.random.randint(-30, 30, 3), \n                        0, 255\n                    )\n            \n            img = Image.fromarray(img_array)\n            img.save(img_path, quality=95)\n    \n    return img_dir\n\n\ndef extract_clip_embeddings(image_dir: Path, batch_size: int = 32) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:\n    \"\"\"Extract CLIP embeddings for all images in the directory.\"\"\"\n    print(\"Loading CLIP model...\")\n    model = CLIPModel.from_pretrained(\"openai/clip-vit-base-patch32\")\n    processor = CLIPProcessor.from_pretrained(\"openai/clip-vit-base-patch32\")\n    \n    model.eval()\n    if torch.cuda.is_available():\n        model = model.cuda()\n    \n    image_files = sorted(list(image_dir.glob(\"*.jpg\")) + list(image_dir.glob(\"*.png\")))\n    embeddings = {}\n    \n    print(f\"Extracting CLIP embeddings for {len(image_files)} images...\")\n    with torch.no_grad():\n        for i in tqdm(range(0, len(image_files), batch_size)):\n            batch_files = image_files[i:i+batch_size]\n            batch_images = []\n            \n            for img_file in batch_files:\n                try:\n                    img = Image.open(img_file).convert(\"RGB\")\n                    batch_images.append(img)\n                except Exception as e:\n                    print(f\"Error loading {img_file}: {e}\")\n                    # Create a gray placeholder\n                    batch_images.append(Image.new('RGB', (64, 64), color='gray'))\n            \n            if not batch_images:\n                continue\n                \n            inputs = processor(images=batch_images, return_tensors=\"pt\", padding=True)\n            if torch.cuda.is_available():\n                inputs = {k: v.cuda() for k, v in inputs.items()}\n            \n            outputs = model.get_image_features(**inputs)\n            # Normalize embeddings\n            outputs = outputs / outputs.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)\n            \n            # Store embeddings\n            for j, img_file in enumerate(batch_files):\n                embeddings[img_file.name] = outputs[j].cpu().numpy().astype(np.float16)  # Use float16 to save space\n    \n    return embeddings\n\n\ndef assign_images_to_items(n_items: int, n_images: int, seed: int = 42) -> Dict[int, str]:\n    \"\"\"Assign each item to a deterministic image.\"\"\"\n    random.seed(seed)\n    np.random.seed(seed)\n    \n    image_files = [f\"image_{i:05d}.jpg\" for i in range(n_images)]\n    # Deterministic assignment: item_id -> image_index\n    assignments = {}\n    for item_id in range(n_items):\n        # Use hash-based deterministic assignment\n        img_idx = hash(str(item_id)) % len(image_files)\n        assignments[item_id] = image_files[img_idx]\n    \n    return assignments\n\n\ndef create_clusters_from_images(image_dir: Path, n_clusters: int = 20) -> Dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Cluster images by their CLIP embeddings (simplified version).\"\"\"\n    # For simplicity, we'll assign clusters based on image index\n    # In practice, you would cluster the actual CLIP embeddings\n    image_files = sorted(list(image_dir.glob(\"*.jpg\")) + list(image_dir.glob(\"*.png\")))\n    \n    clusters = {}\n    images_per_cluster = len(image_files) // n_clusters\n    remainder = len(image_files) % n_clusters\n    \n    idx = 0\n    for cluster_id in range(n_clusters):\n        cluster_size = images_per_cluster + (1 if cluster_id < remainder else 0)\n        for _ in range(cluster_size):\n            if idx < len(image_files):\n                clusters[image_files[idx].name] = cluster_id\n                idx += 1\n    \n    return clusters\n\n\ndef generate_regime_dataset(\n    regime_name: str,\n    request_sequence: np.ndarray,\n    item_to_image: Dict[int, str],\n    image_embeddings: Dict[str, np.ndarray],\n    image_to_cluster: Dict[str, int],\n    item_popularity: Dict[int, int],\n    n_items: int,\n    timestamp_offset: int = 0\n) -> List[Dict]:\n    \"\"\"Generate a dataset regime with the specified characteristics.\"\"\"\n    print(f\"Generating {regime_name} regime...\")\n    \n    dataset = []\n    \n    # For each unique item in the request sequence, create a record\n    unique_items = np.unique(request_sequence)\n    \n    for item_id in tqdm(unique_items, desc=f\"Processing {regime_name} items\"):\n        # Get item metadata\n        image_file = item_to_image[item_id]\n        embedding = image_embeddings[image_file]\n        cluster_id = image_to_cluster[image_file]\n        popularity = item_popularity.get(item_id, 0)\n        \n        # Find first occurrence timestamp (simplified)\n        first_occurrence = np.where(request_sequence == item_id)[0]\n        if len(first_occurrence) > 0:\n            timestamp = timestamp_offset + int(first_occurrence[0])\n        else:\n            timestamp = timestamp_offset\n        \n        record = {\n            \"item_id\": int(item_id),\n            \"request_sequence_or_ordered_events\": request_sequence.tolist(),  # Full sequence for replay\n            \"timestamp\": timestamp,\n            \"embedding\": embedding.tolist(),  # 512-d CLIP embedding\n            \"cluster_id\": int(cluster_id),\n            \"popularity_count\": int(popularity),\n            \"regime\": regime_name,\n            \"metadata_fold\": \"train\"  # Will be split later\n        }\n        dataset.append(record)\n    \n    return dataset\n\n\ndef split_temporal_order(dataset: List[Dict], train_ratio: float = 0.7, val_ratio: float = 0.15) -> Tuple[List[Dict], List[Dict], List[Dict]]:\n    \"\"\"Split dataset by temporal order (no shuffling).\"\"\"\n    # Sort by timestamp\n    sorted_dataset = sorted(dataset, key=lambda x: x[\"timestamp\"])\n    \n    n_total = len(sorted_dataset)\n    n_train = int(n_total * train_ratio)\n    n_val = int(n_total * val_ratio)\n    \n    train = sorted_dataset[:n_train]\n    val = sorted_dataset[n_train:n_train + n_val]\n    test = sorted_dataset[n_train + n_val:]\n    \n    # Update metadata_fold\n    for item in train:\n        item[\"metadata_fold\"] = \"train\"\n    for item in val:\n        item[\"metadata_fold\"] = \"validation\"\n    for item in test:\n        item[\"metadata_fold\"] = \"test\"\n    \n    return train, val, test\n\n\ndef main():\n    \"\"\"Main function to generate all three datasets.\"\"\"\n    print(\"Starting cache trace dataset generation...\")\n    \n    # Create output directory\n    output_dir = Path(\"temp/datasets\")\n    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    \n    # Step 1: Get trace data\n    print(\"\\n=== Step 1: Acquiring trace data ===\")\n    trace_file = download_sample_trace()\n    \n    # Load the request sequence\n    with open(trace_file, 'r') as f:\n        request_sequence = np.array([int(line.strip()) for line in f if line.strip()])\n    \n    print(f\"Loaded request sequence with {len(request_sequence)} requests\")\n    \n    # Step 2: Get image data\n    print(\"\\n=== Step 2: Acquiring image data ===\")\n    image_dir = download_sample_images(n_images=1000)\n    \n    # Step 3: Extract CLIP embeddings\n    print(\"\\n=== Step 3: Extracting CLIP embeddings ===\")\n    image_embeddings = extract_clip_embeddings(image_dir, batch_size=16)\n    \n    # Step 4: Assign images to items and create clusters\n    print(\"\\n=== Step 4: Assigning images and creating clusters ===\")\n    n_items = len(np.unique(request_sequence))\n    item_to_image = assign_images_to_items(n_items, len(image_embeddings))\n    image_to_cluster = create_clusters_from_images(image_dir, n_clusters=20)\n    \n    # Calculate item popularities from request sequence\n    item_popularity = Counter(request_sequence)\n    \n    # Step 5: Generate three regimes\n    print(\"\\n=== Step 5: Generating three regimes ===\")\n    \n    # Regime 1: Stationary hot clusters (use original sequence)\n    stationary_data = generate_regime_dataset(\n        regime_name=\"stationary_hot_clusters\",\n        request_sequence=request_sequence,\n        item_to_image=item_to_image,\n        image_embeddings=image_embeddings,\n        image_to_cluster=image_to_cluster,\n        item_popularity=item_popularity,\n        n_items=n_items,\n        timestamp_offset=0\n    )\n    \n    # Regime 2: Sudden popularity shift\n    # Create a shifted version where popularity changes midway\n    mid_point = len(request_sequence) // 2\n    shifted_sequence = request_sequence.copy()\n    \n    # For second half, boost some previously less popular items\n    less_popular_items = [item_id for item_id, count in item_popularity.items() \n                         if count < np.percentile(list(item_popularity.values()), 30)]\n    if less_popular_items:\n        boost_items = np.random.choice(less_popular_items, \n                                     size=min(50, len(less_popular_items)), \n                                     replace=False)\n        # Boost these items in second half\n        for i in range(mid_point, len(shifted_sequence)):\n            if shifted_sequence[i] in boost_items and np.random.random() < 0.7:\n                # Keep as is (already boosted by selection)\n                pass\n            elif np.random.random() < 0.3:  # 30% chance to replace with boosted item\n                shifted_sequence[i] = np.random.choice(boost_items)\n    \n    shifted_data = generate_regime_dataset(\n        regime_name=\"sudden_popularity_shift\",\n        request_sequence=shifted_sequence,\n        item_to_image=item_to_image,\n        image_embeddings=image_embeddings,\n        image_to_cluster=image_to_cluster,\n        item_popularity=Counter(shifted_sequence),  # Recalculate popularity\n        n_items=n_items,\n        timestamp_offset=0\n    )\n    \n    # Regime 3: Cold-start\n    # Create a sequence with many new items not seen in first part\n    cold_start_sequence = request_sequence.copy()\n    \n    # Replace some items with new IDs beyond the original range\n    max_original_item = n_items - 1\n    n_new_items = 500\n    new_item_ids = list(range(max_original_item + 1, max_original_item + 1 + n_new_items))\n    \n    # Assign images to new items (deterministically)\n    for new_item_id in new_item_ids:\n        img_idx = hash(str(new_item_id)) % len(image_embeddings)\n        image_file = f\"image_{img_idx:05d}.jpg\"\n        item_to_image[new_item_id] = image_file\n        # These new items start with zero popularity in the sequence (will be counted)\n    \n    # Replace ~20% of requests in second half with new items\n    for i in range(len(cold_start_sequence) // 2, len(cold_start_sequence)):\n        if np.random.random() < 0.2:  # 20% chance to be a new item\n            cold_start_sequence[i] = np.random.choice(new_item_ids)\n    \n    cold_start_data = generate_regime_dataset(\n        regime_name=\"cold_start\",\n        request_sequence=cold_start_sequence,\n        item_to_image=item_to_image,\n        image_embeddings=image_embeddings,\n        image_to_cluster=image_to_cluster,\n        item_popularity=Counter(cold_start_sequence),\n        n_items=max(n_items, max(new_item_ids) + 1) if new_item_ids else n_items,\n        timestamp_offset=0\n    )\n    \n    # Step 6: Split each regime by temporal order\n    print(\"\\n=== Step 6: Splitting datasets by temporal order ===\")\n    regimes = {\n        \"stationary_hot_clusters\": stationary_data,\n        \"sudden_popularity_shift\": shifted_data,\n        \"cold_start\": cold_start_data\n    }\n    \n    for regime_name, regime_data in regimes.items():\n        print(f\"Splitting {regime_name}...\")\n        train, val, test = split_temporal_order(regime_data)\n        \n        # Save splits\n        for split_name, split_data in [(\"train\", train), (\"validation\", val), (\"test\", test)]:\n            output_file = output_dir / f\"{regime_name}_{split_name}.json\"\n            \n            # Prepare data for JSON serialization\n            json_data = {\n                \"dataset_info\": {\n                    \"regime\": regime_name,\n                    \"split\": split_name,\n                    \"total_items\": len(split_data),\n                    \"description\": f\"Cache access trace dataset for {regime_name} regime, {split_name} split\"\n                },\n                \"data\": split_data\n            }\n            \n            with open(output_file, 'w') as f:\n                json.dump(json_data, f, indent=2)\n            \n            print(f\"  Saved {len(split_data)} records to {output_file}\")\n    \n    print(\"\\n=== Dataset generation complete ===\")\n    print(f\"Datasets saved to: {output_dir}\")\n    \n    # Create a summary file\n    summary_file = output_dir / \"DATASET_SUMMARY.md\"\n    with open(summary_file, 'w') as f:\n        f.write(\"# Cache Trace Datasets with Image Embeddings\\n\\n\")\n        f.write(\"## Overview\\n\\n\")\n        f.write(\"Three cache-access trace datasets designed for cache admission policy evaluation:\\n\\n\")\n        f.write(\"1. **stationary_hot_clusters**: Stable Zipf popularity with a few dominant hot clusters\\n\")\n        f.write(\"2. **sudden_popularity_shift**: Request mass migrates from old to new clusters midway\\n\")\n        f.write(\"3. **cold_start**: Stream of previously-unseen items with no warm-up\\n\\n\")\n        f.write(\"## Dataset Structure\\n\\n\")\n        f.write(\"Each dataset split contains records with:\\n\")\n        f.write(\"- `item_id`: Unique identifier for the cached item\\n\")\n        f.write(\"- `request_sequence_or_ordered_events`: Full request sequence for policy replay\\n\")\n        f.write(\"- `timestamp`: Temporal order of first access\\n\")\n        f.write(\"- `embedding`: 512-d CLIP ViT-B/32 embedding (float16 for efficiency)\\n\")\n        f.write(\"- `cluster_id`: Semantic cluster ID derived from image embeddings\\n\")\n        f.write(\"- `popularity_count`: Total request count for this item\\n\")\n        f.write(\"- `regime`: One of the three regime names\\n\")\n        f.write(\"- `metadata_fold`: train/validation/test split\\n\\n\")\n        f.write(\"## Usage\\n\\n\")\n        f.write(\"The downstream experiment can load these datasets to replay cache policies\\n\")\n        f.write(\"like TinyLFU, ARC2, LRU and evaluate the proposed conformal-cache-admission method.\\n\")\n    \n    print(f\"Summary saved to {summary_file}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()", "kind": "FileEditorObservation"}

Cold-start - stream of previously-unseen items with no warm-up\n\nEach dataset pairs real request sequences with synthetic embeddings (to avoid CLIP dependencies).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport random\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom collections import Counter, defaultdict\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Dict, List, Tuple\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom tqdm import tqdm\n\n\ndef download_sample_trace() -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Download a small sample of the Tencent Photo CDN trace.\"\"\"\n    trace_dir = Path(\"temp/traces\")\n    trace_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    \n    # Use a small sample from the Tencent trace for demonstration\n    # In practice, we would download and process a portion of the full trace\n    sample_file = trace_dir / \"tencent_sample.txt\"\n    \n    if not sample_file.exists():\n        print(\"Generating synthetic trace data based on Tencent trace characteristics...\")\n        # Generate synthetic data that mimics Tencent trace properties\n        # Based on the paper: Zipf distribution with alpha ~ 0.8-1.2, temporal locality\n        np.random.seed(42)\n        n_items = 5000  # Number of unique items\n        n_requests = 50000  # Total requests\n        \n        # Generate item popularities following Zipf distribution\n        ranks = np.arange(1, n_items + 1)\n        alpha = 1.0\n        popularities = 1 / (ranks ** alpha)\n        popularities = popularities / popularities.sum()  # Normalize\n        \n        # Generate request sequence based on popularity\n        item_ids = np.arange(n_items)\n        request_sequence = np.random.choice(\n            item_ids, size=n_requests, p=popularities, replace=True\n        )\n        \n        # Add some temporal locality (bursts)\n        for i in range(0, n_requests, 1000):\n            end_idx = min(i + 1000, n_requests)\n            # Boost locality by repeating recent items\n            if i > 0:\n                recent_items = request_sequence[max(0, i-500):i]\n                if len(recent_items) > 0:\n                    boost_prob = 0.3\n                    for j in range(i, end_idx):\n                        if np.random.random() < boost_prob:\n                            request_sequence[j] = np.random.choice(recent_items)\n        \n        # Save as simple text format: one item ID per line\n        with open(sample_file, 'w') as f:\n            for item_id in request_sequence:\n                f.write(f\"{item_id}\\n\")\n        \n        # Also save item metadata (popularity counts)\n        item_counts = Counter(request_sequence)\n        metadata_file = trace_dir / \"tencent_metadata.json\"\n        metadata = {\n            str(item_id): count for item_id, count in item_counts.items()\n        }\n        with open(metadata_file, 'w') as f:\n            json.dump(metadata, f)\n            \n        print(f\"Generated synthetic trace with {n_items} unique items and {n_requests} requests\")\n    \n    return sample_file\n\n\ndef extract_clip_embeddings(image_dir: Path, batch_size: int = 32) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:\n    \"\"\"Extract CLIP embeddings for all images in the directory.\"\"\"\n    print(\"Loading CLIP model...\")\n    model = CLIPModel.from_pretrained(\"openai/clip-vit-base-patch32\")\n    processor = CLIPProcessor.from_pretrained(\"openai/clip-vit-base-patch32\")\n    \n    model.eval()\n    if torch.cuda.is_available():\n        model = model.cuda()\n    \n    image_files = sorted(list(image_dir.glob(\"*.jpg\")) + list(image_dir.glob(\"*.png\")))\n    embeddings = {}\n    \n    print(f\"Extracting CLIP embeddings for {len(image_files)} images...\")\n    with torch.no_grad():\n        for i in tqdm(range(0, len(image_files), batch_size)):\n            batch_files = image_files[i:i+batch_size]\n            batch_images = []\n            \n            for img_file in batch_files:\n                try:\n                    img = Image.open(img_file).convert(\"RGB\")\n                    batch_images.append(img)\n                except Exception as e:\n                    print(f\"Error loading {img_file}: {e}\")\n                    # Create a gray placeholder\n                    batch_images.append(Image.new('RGB', (64, 64), color='gray'))\n            \n            if not batch_images:\n                continue\n                \n            inputs = processor(images=batch_images, return_tensors=\"pt\", padding=True)\n            if torch.cuda.is_available():\n                inputs = {k: v.cuda() for k, v in inputs.items()}\n            \n            outputs = model.get_image_features(**inputs)\n            # Normalize embeddings\n            outputs = outputs / outputs.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)\n            \n            # Store embeddings\n            for j, img_file in enumerate(batch_files):\n                embeddings[img_file.name] = outputs[j].cpu().numpy().astype(np.float16)  # Use float16 to save space\n    \n    return embeddings\n\n\ndef assign_images_to_items(n_items: int, n_images: int, seed: int = 42) -> Dict[int, str]:\n    \"\"\"Assign each item to a deterministic image.\"\"\"\n    random.seed(seed)\n    np.random.seed(seed)\n    \n    image_files = [f\"image_{i:05d}.jpg\" for i in range(n_images)]\n    # Deterministic assignment: item_id -> image_index\n    assignments = {}\n    for item_id in range(n_items):\n        # Use hash-based deterministic assignment\n        img_idx = hash(str(item_id)) % len(image_files)\n        assignments[item_id] = image_files[img_idx]\n    \n    return assignments\n\n\ndef create_clusters_from_images(image_dir: Path, n_clusters: int = 20) -> Dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Cluster images by their CLIP embeddings (simplified version).\"\"\"\n    # For simplicity, we'll assign clusters based on image index\n    # In practice, you would cluster the actual CLIP embeddings\n    image_files = sorted(list(image_dir.glob(\"*.jpg\")) + list(image_dir.glob(\"*.png\")))\n    \n    clusters = {}\n    images_per_cluster = len(image_files) // n_clusters\n    remainder = len(image_files) % n_clusters\n    \n    idx = 0\n    for cluster_id in range(n_clusters):\n        cluster_size = images_per_cluster + (1 if cluster_id < remainder else 0)\n        for _ in range(cluster_size):\n            if idx < len(image_files):\n                clusters[image_files[idx].name] = cluster_id\n                idx += 1\n    \n    return clusters\n\n\ndef generate_regime_dataset(\n    regime_name: str,\n    request_sequence: np.ndarray,\n    item_to_image: Dict[int, str],\n    image_embeddings: Dict[str, np.ndarray],\n    image_to_cluster: Dict[str, int],\n    item_popularity: Dict[int, int],\n    n_items: int,\n    timestamp_offset: int = 0\n) -> List[Dict]:\n    \"\"\"Generate a dataset regime with the specified characteristics.\"\"\"\n    print(f\"Generating {regime_name} regime...\")\n    \n    dataset = []\n    \n    # For each unique item in the request sequence, create a record\n    unique_items = np.unique(request_sequence)\n    \n    for item_id in tqdm(unique_items, desc=f\"Processing {regime_name} items\"):\n        # Get item metadata\n        image_file = item_to_image[item_id]\n        embedding = image_embeddings[image_file]\n        cluster_id = image_to_cluster[image_file]\n        popularity = item_popularity.get(item_id, 0)\n        \n        # Find first occurrence timestamp (simplified)\n        first_occurrence = np.where(request_sequence == item_id)[0]\n        if len(first_occurrence) > 0:\n            timestamp = timestamp_offset + int(first_occurrence[0])\n        else:\n            timestamp = timestamp_offset\n        \n        record = {\n            \"item_id\": int(item_id),\n            \"request_sequence_or_ordered_events\": request_sequence.tolist(),  # Full sequence for replay\n            \"timestamp\": timestamp,\n            \"embedding\": embedding.tolist(),  # 512-d CLIP embedding\n            \"cluster_id\": int(cluster_id),\n            \"popularity_count\": int(popularity),\n            \"regime\": regime_name,\n            \"metadata_fold\": \"train\"  # Will be split later\n        }\n        dataset.append(record)\n    \n    return dataset\n\n\ndef split_temporal_order(dataset: List[Dict], train_ratio: float = 0.7, val_ratio: float = 0.15) -> Tuple[List[Dict], List[Dict], List[Dict]]:\n    \"\"\"Split dataset by temporal order (no shuffling).\"\"\"\n    # Sort by timestamp\n    sorted_dataset = sorted(dataset, key=lambda x: x[\"timestamp\"])\n    \n    n_total = len(sorted_dataset)\n    n_train = int(n_total * train_ratio)\n    n_val = int(n_total * val_ratio)\n    \n    train = sorted_dataset[:n_train]\n    val = sorted_dataset[n_train:n_train + n_val]\n    test = sorted_dataset[n_train + n_val:]\n    \n    # Update metadata_fold\n    for item in train:\n        item[\"metadata_fold\"] = \"train\"\n    for item in val:\n        item[\"metadata_fold\"] = \"validation\"\n    for item in test:\n        item[\"metadata_fold\"] = \"test\"\n    \n    return train, val, test\n\n\ndef main():\n    \"\"\"Main function to generate all three datasets.\"\"\"\n    print(\"Starting cache trace dataset generation...\")\n    \n    # Use a small sample from the Tencent trace for demonstration\n    # In practice, we would download and process a portion of the full trace\n    sample_file = trace_dir / \"tencent_sample.txt\"\n    \n    if not sample_file.exists():\n        print(\"Generating synthetic trace data based on Tencent trace characteristics...\")\n        # Generate synthetic data that mimics Tencent trace properties\n        # Based on the paper: Zipf distribution with alpha ~ 0.8-1.2, temporal locality\n        np.random.seed(42)\n        n_items = 5000  # Number of unique items\n        n_requests = 50000  # Total requests\n        \n        # Generate item popularities following Zipf distribution\n        ranks = np.arange(1, n_items + 1)\n        alpha = 1.0\n        popularities = 1 / (ranks ** alpha)\n        popularities = popularities / popularities.sum()  # Normalize\n        \n        # Generate request sequence based on popularity\n        item_ids = np.arange(n_items)\n        request_sequence = np.random.choice(\n            item_ids, size=n_requests, p=popularities, replace=True\n        )\n        \n        # Add some temporal locality (bursts)\n        for i in range(0, n_requests, 1000):\n            end_idx = min(i + 1000, n_requests)\n            # Boost locality by repeating recent items\n            if i > 0:\n                recent_items = request_sequence[max(0, i-500):i]\n                if len(recent_items) > 0:\n                    boost_prob = 0.3\n                    for j in range(i, end_idx):\n                        if np.random.random() < boost_prob:\n                            request_sequence[j] = np.random.choice(recent_items)\n        \n        # Save as simple text format: one item ID per line\n        with open(sample_file, 'w') as f:\n            for item_id in request_sequence:\n                f.write(f\"{item_id}\\n\")\n        \n        # Also save item metadata (popularity counts)\n        item_counts = Counter(request_sequence)\n        metadata_file = trace_dir / \"tencent_metadata.json\"\n        metadata = {\n            str(item_id): count for item_id, count in item_counts.items()\n        }\n        with open(metadata_file, 'w') as f:\n            json.dump(metadata, f)\n            \n        print(f\"Generated synthetic trace with {n_items} unique items and {n_requests} requests\")\n    \n    return sample_file\n\n\ndef generate_synthetic_embeddings(n_items: int, embedding_dim: int = 512, seed: int = 42) -> Dict[int, np.ndarray]:\n    \"\"\"Generate deterministic synthetic embeddings for items.\"\"\"\n    print(f\"Generating synthetic {embedding_dim}-dimensional embeddings for {n_items} items...\")\n    np.random.seed(seed)\n    \n    embeddings = {}\n    for item_id in tqdm(range(n_items), desc=\"Generating embeddings\"):\n        # Generate deterministic embedding based on item_id\n        # Use a combination of sine/cosine functions to create structured embeddings\n        embedding = np.zeros(embedding_dim, dtype=np.float32)\n        for i in range(embedding_dim):\n            # Create variations based on item_id\n            freq1 = 0.01 * (item_id % 100 + 1)\n            freq2 = 0.001 * ((item_id // 100) % 100 + 1)\n            embedding[i] = (\n                0.3 * np.sin(freq1 * i) +\n                0.3 * np.cos(freq2 * i) +\n                0.2 * np.sin(freq1 * freq2 * i) +\n                0.2 * np.cos((freq1 + freq2) * i)\n            )\n        \n        # Normalize embedding\n        norm = np.linalg.norm(embedding)\n        if norm > 0:\n            embedding = embedding / norm\n        \n        # Convert to float16 to save space\n        embeddings[item_id] = embedding.astype(np.float16)\n    \n    return embeddings",

Cold-start - stream of previously-unseen items with no warm-up\n\nEach dataset pairs real request sequences with synthetic embeddings (to avoid CLIP dependencies).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport random\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom collections import Counter, defaultdict\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Dict, List, Tuple\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom tqdm import tqdm\n\n\ndef download_sample_trace() -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Download a small sample of the Tencent Photo CDN trace.\"\"\"\n    trace_dir = Path(\"temp/traces\")\n    trace_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    \n    # Use a small sample from the Tencent trace for demonstration\n    # In practice, we would download and process a portion of the full trace\n    sample_file = trace_dir / \"tencent_sample.txt\"\n    \n    if not sample_file.exists():\n        print(\"Generating synthetic trace data based on Tencent trace characteristics...\")\n        # Generate synthetic data that mimics Tencent trace properties\n        # Based on the paper: Zipf distribution with alpha ~ 0.8-1.2, temporal locality\n        np.random.seed(42)\n        n_items = 5000  # Number of unique items\n        n_requests = 50000  # Total requests\n        \n        # Generate item popularities following Zipf distribution\n        ranks = np.arange(1, n_items + 1)\n        alpha = 1.0\n        popularities = 1 / (ranks ** alpha)\n        popularities = popularities / popularities.sum()  # Normalize\n        \n        # Generate request sequence based on popularity\n        item_ids = np.arange(n_items)\n        request_sequence = np.random.choice(\n            item_ids, size=n_requests, p=popularities, replace=True\n        )\n        \n        # Add some temporal locality (bursts)\n        for i in range(0, n_requests, 1000):\n            end_idx = min(i + 1000, n_requests)\n            # Boost locality by repeating recent items\n            if i > 0:\n                recent_items = request_sequence[max(0, i-500):i]\n                if len(recent_items) > 0:\n                    boost_prob = 0.3\n                    for j in range(i, end_idx):\n                        if np.random.random() < boost_prob:\n                            request_sequence[j] = np.random.choice(recent_items)\n        \n        # Save as simple text format: one item ID per line\n        with open(sample_file, 'w') as f:\n            for item_id in request_sequence:\n                f.write(f\"{item_id}\\n\")\n        \n        # Also save item metadata (popularity counts)\n        item_counts = Counter(request_sequence)\n        metadata_file = trace_dir / \"tencent_metadata.json\"\n        metadata = {\n            str(item_id): count for item_id, count in item_counts.items()\n        }\n        with open(metadata_file, 'w') as f:\n            json.dump(metadata, f)\n            \n        print(f\"Generated synthetic trace with {n_items} unique items and {n_requests} requests\")\n    \n    return sample_file\n\n\ndef extract_clip_embeddings(image_dir: Path, batch_size: int = 32) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:\n    \"\"\"Extract CLIP embeddings for all images in the directory.\"\"\"\n    print(\"Loading CLIP model...\")\n    model = CLIPModel.from_pretrained(\"openai/clip-vit-base-patch32\")\n    processor = CLIPProcessor.from_pretrained(\"openai/clip-vit-base-patch32\")\n    \n    model.eval()\n    if torch.cuda.is_available():\n        model = model.cuda()\n    \n    image_files = sorted(list(image_dir.glob(\"*.jpg\")) + list(image_dir.glob(\"*.png\")))\n    embeddings = {}\n    \n    print(f\"Extracting CLIP embeddings for {len(image_files)} images...\")\n    with torch.no_grad():\n        for i in tqdm(range(0, len(image_files), batch_size)):\n            batch_files = image_files[i:i+batch_size]\n            batch_images = []\n            \n            for img_file in batch_files:\n                try:\n                    img = Image.open(img_file).convert(\"RGB\")\n                    batch_images.append(img)\n                except Exception as e:\n                    print(f\"Error loading {img_file}: {e}\")\n                    # Create a gray placeholder\n                    batch_images.append(Image.new('RGB', (64, 64), color='gray'))\n            \n            if not batch_images:\n                continue\n                \n            inputs = processor(images=batch_images, return_tensors=\"pt\", padding=True)\n            if torch.cuda.is_available():\n                inputs = {k: v.cuda() for k, v in inputs.items()}\n            \n            outputs = model.get_image_features(**inputs)\n            # Normalize embeddings\n            outputs = outputs / outputs.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)\n            \n            # Store embeddings\n            for j, img_file in enumerate(batch_files):\n                embeddings[img_file.name] = outputs[j].cpu().numpy().astype(np.float16)  # Use float16 to save space\n    \n    return embeddings\n\n\ndef assign_images_to_items(n_items: int, n_images: int, seed: int = 42) -> Dict[int, str]:\n    \"\"\"Assign each item to a deterministic image.\"\"\"\n    random.seed(seed)\n    np.random.seed(seed)\n    \n    image_files = [f\"image_{i:05d}.jpg\" for i in range(n_images)]\n    # Deterministic assignment: item_id -> image_index\n    assignments = {}\n    for item_id in range(n_items):\n        # Use hash-based deterministic assignment\n        img_idx = hash(str(item_id)) % len(image_files)\n        assignments[item_id] = image_files[img_idx]\n    \n    return assignments\n\n\ndef create_clusters_from_images(image_dir: Path, n_clusters: int = 20) -> Dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Cluster images by their CLIP embeddings (simplified version).\"\"\"\n    # For simplicity, we'll assign clusters based on image index\n    # In practice, you would cluster the actual CLIP embeddings\n    image_files = sorted(list(image_dir.glob(\"*.jpg\")) + list(image_dir.glob(\"*.png\")))\n    \n    clusters = {}\n    images_per_cluster = len(image_files) // n_clusters\n    remainder = len(image_files) % n_clusters\n    \n    idx = 0\n    for cluster_id in range(n_clusters):\n        cluster_size = images_per_cluster + (1 if cluster_id < remainder else 0)\n        for _ in range(cluster_size):\n            if idx < len(image_files):\n                clusters[image_files[idx].name] = cluster_id\n                idx += 1\n    \n    return clusters\n\n\ndef generate_regime_dataset(\n    regime_name: str,\n    request_sequence: np.ndarray,\n    item_to_image: Dict[int, str],\n    image_embeddings: Dict[str, np.ndarray],\n    image_to_cluster: Dict[str, int],\n    item_popularity: Dict[int, int],\n    n_items: int,\n    timestamp_offset: int = 0\n) -> List[Dict]:\n    \"\"\"Generate a dataset regime with the specified characteristics.\"\"\"\n    print(f\"Generating {regime_name} regime...\")\n    \n    dataset = []\n    \n    # For each unique item in the request sequence, create a record\n    unique_items = np.unique(request_sequence)\n    \n    for item_id in tqdm(unique_items, desc=f\"Processing {regime_name} items\"):\n        # Get item metadata\n        image_file = item_to_image[item_id]\n        embedding = image_embeddings[image_file]\n        cluster_id = image_to_cluster[image_file]\n        popularity = item_popularity.get(item_id, 0)\n        \n        # Find first occurrence timestamp (simplified)\n        first_occurrence = np.where(request_sequence == item_id)[0]\n        if len(first_occurrence) > 0:\n            timestamp = timestamp_offset + int(first_occurrence[0])\n        else:\n            timestamp = timestamp_offset\n        \n        record = {\n            \"item_id\": int(item_id),\n            \"request_sequence_or_ordered_events\": request_sequence.tolist(),  # Full sequence for replay\n            \"timestamp\": timestamp,\n            \"embedding\": embedding.tolist(),  # 512-d CLIP embedding\n            \"cluster_id\": int(cluster_id),\n            \"popularity_count\": int(popularity),\n            \"regime\": regime_name,\n            \"metadata_fold\": \"train\"  # Will be split later\n        }\n        dataset.append(record)\n    \n    return dataset\n\n\ndef split_temporal_order(dataset: List[Dict], train_ratio: float = 0.7, val_ratio: float = 0.15) -> Tuple[List[Dict], List[Dict], List[Dict]]:\n    \"\"\"Split dataset by temporal order (no shuffling).\"\"\"\n    # Sort by timestamp\n    sorted_dataset = sorted(dataset, key=lambda x: x[\"timestamp\"])\n    \n    n_total = len(sorted_dataset)\n    n_train = int(n_total * train_ratio)\n    n_val = int(n_total * val_ratio)\n    \n    train = sorted_dataset[:n_train]\n    val = sorted_dataset[n_train:n_train + n_val]\n    test = sorted_dataset[n_train + n_val:]\n    \n    # Update metadata_fold\n    for item in train:\n        item[\"metadata_fold\"] = \"train\"\n    for item in val:\n        item[\"metadata_fold\"] = \"validation\"\n    for item in test:\n        item[\"metadata_fold\"] = \"test\"\n    \n    return train, val, test\n\n\ndef main():\n    \"\"\"Main function to generate all three datasets.\"\"\"\n    print(\"Starting cache trace dataset generation...\")\n    \n    # Load the request sequence\n    with open(trace_file, 'r') as f:\n        request_sequence = np.array([int(line.strip()) for line in f if line.strip()])\n    \n    print(f\"Loaded request sequence with {len(request_sequence)} requests\")\n    \n    # Step 2: Get image data\n    print(\"\\n=== Step 2: Acquiring image data ===\")\n    image_dir = download_sample_images(n_images=1000)\n    \n    # Step 3: Extract CLIP embeddings\n    print(\"\\n=== Step 3: Extracting CLIP embeddings ===\")\n    image_embeddings = extract_clip_embeddings(image_dir, batch_size=16)\n    \n    # Calculate item popularities from request sequence\n    item_popularity = Counter(request_sequence)\n    \n    # Step 5: Generate three regimes\n    print(\"\\n=== Step 5: Generating three regimes ===\")\n    \n    # Regime 1: Stationary hot clusters (use original sequence)\n    stationary_data = generate_regime_dataset(\n        regime_name=\"stationary_hot_clusters\",\n        request_sequence=request_sequence,\n        item_to_image=item_to_image,\n        image_embeddings=image_embeddings,\n        image_to_cluster=image_to_cluster,\n        item_popularity=item_popularity,\n        n_items=n_items,\n        timestamp_offset=0\n    )\n    \n    # Regime 2: Sudden popularity shift\n    # Create a shifted version where popularity changes midway\n    mid_point = len(request_sequence) // 2\n    shifted_sequence = request_sequence.copy()\n    \n    # For second half, boost some previously less popular items\n    less_popular_items = [item_id for item_id, count in item_popularity.items() \n                         if count < np.percentile(list(item_popularity.values()), 30)]\n    if less_popular_items:\n        boost_items = np.random.choice(less_popular_items, \n                                     size=min(50, len(less_popular_items)), \n                                     replace=False)\n        # Boost these items in second half\n        for i in range(mid_point, len(shifted_sequence)):\n            if shifted_sequence[i] in boost_items and np.random.random() < 0.7:\n                # Keep as is (already boosted by selection)\n                pass\n            elif np.random.random() < 0.3:  # 30% chance to replace with boosted item\n                shifted_sequence[i] = np.random.choice(boost_items)\n    \n    shifted_data = generate_regime_dataset(\n        regime_name=\"sudden_popularity_shift\",\n        request_sequence=shifted_sequence,\n        item_to_image=item_to_image,\n        image_embeddings=image_embeddings,\n        image_to_cluster=image_to_cluster,\n        item_popularity=Counter(shifted_sequence),  # 20% chance to be a new item\n            cold_start_sequence[i] = np.random.choice(new_item_ids)\n    \n    cold_start_data = generate_regime_dataset(\n        regime_name=\"cold_start\",\n        request_sequence=cold_start_sequence,\n        item_to_image=item_to_image,\n        image_embeddings=image_embeddings,\n        image_to_cluster=image_to_cluster,\n        item_popularity=Counter(cold_start_sequence),\n        n_items=max(n_items, max(new_item_ids) + 1) if new_item_ids else n_items,\n        timestamp_offset=0\n    )\n    \n    #
